metadata.description: Maps notebook functions to curriculum nodes. Each function appears in 1-3 notebooks with increasing DOF complexity. The tutor uses this map to find the right code reference for the current module and node.

uelXXX.description: Element stiffness matrix computation. The core function that defines each element type.

pedagogical_role: MODEL: show the simplest stiffness matrix
GUIDED_PRACTICE: student compares their hand-derived K to this code
COACHING: verify student's numerical answers
MODEL: show how K_local, Q (transformation), and K_global are computed in one function
COACHING: student traces through the code to identify where K_local ends and transformation begins
ARTICULATION: ask student to explain each line
nb02.note: This function combines local K, builds Q, and transforms in one shot — the tutor should decompose it into the 3 separate curriculum steps

pedagogical_role: MODEL: show the full frame pipeline (K_local → Q → K_global)
COACHING: student identifies the 4×4 beam K inside the code
ARTICULATION: ask why Q has the specific structure it does
nb03.note: Frame notebook uses beam WITHOUT axial DOFs (4×4 local, 6×6 global via Q). This differs from our curriculum which builds the full 6×6 frame element. The tutor should note this difference explicitly.

uelXXX.cross_module_narrative: The element function evolves: uelspring builds a 2×2 directly. ueltruss2D builds a 2×2 local, constructs Q, transforms to 4×4 global. uelbeam2DU builds a 4×4 beam local, constructs Q, transforms to 6×6 global. The pattern is always: local K → transformation → global K. Only the sizes grow.

eqcounter.description: Reads boundary condition flags from node data and assigns equation numbers to free DOFs. This IS the IBC array construction.

pedagogical_role: MODEL: show how -1 flags become the IBC array
COACHING: student traces through for a specific example
MODEL: show the 2-DOF generalization
ARTICULATION: ask student what changed from the spring version and why
MODEL: show the 3-DOF generalization
REFLECTION: student compares all 3 versions side-by-side

eqcounter.cross_module_narrative: eqcounter scales from 1 to 2 to 3 columns — one per DOF. The logic is identical: scan for 0 (free) vs -1 (restrained), assign sequential equation numbers to free DOFs. This is the IBC array the curriculum teaches. The student should recognize that the SAME algorithm handles springs, trusses, and frames — only the number of DOFs per node changes.

DME.description: Builds the assembly operator — maps element local DOFs to global equation numbers using the IBC array and element connectivity.

pedagogical_role: MODEL: show the connectivity mapping from local to global
COACHING: student builds DME by hand then compares to code output
MODEL: show 4-DOF per element mapping
ARTICULATION: ask student to explain the inner loop over 2 DOFs per node
MODEL: show 6-DOF per element mapping
REFLECTION: compare all 3 DME implementations

DME.cross_module_narrative: DME grows from nels×2 to nels×4 to nels×6 — the number of columns equals the element DOFs. The inner loop iterates over DOFs per node (1, 2, or 3). This is the concrete implementation of the local-to-global DOF mapping the curriculum teaches. The pattern is: for each element, for each node, for each DOF at that node, look up the equation number in IBC.

assembly.description: Assembles the global stiffness matrix by scattering each element's K_global into the right positions using the DME operator.

pedagogical_role: MODEL: show the scatter-add loop
COACHING: student traces through assembly of a 2-spring system
ARTICULATION: ask why the if glob_row != -1 check is needed
MODEL: same scatter-add with 4×4 element matrices
REFLECTION: compare to spring assembly — what changed?
MODEL: same scatter-add with 6×6 element matrices
REFLECTION: the assembly code is nearly identical across all 3 modules

assembly.cross_module_narrative: The assembly function is IDENTICAL in structure across all 3 notebooks. Only ndof changes (2→4→6). This is the key pedagogical point: assembly is a GENERIC operation. The same double loop (over element rows, over element columns, skip if -1) works for any element type. The student should see that once they understand spring assembly, they understand ALL assembly.

loadasem.description: Assembles the global load vector from applied nodal loads using the IBC array.

pedagogical_role: MODEL: show load placement using IBC
MODEL: 2-component loads (Fx, Fy) placed via IBC
MODEL: 3-component loads (Fx, Fy, M) placed via IBC

loadasem.cross_module_narrative: Load assembly mirrors the DOF scaling: 1 component per node (springs), 2 (trusses), 3 (frames). The logic is: for each loaded node, look up its equation numbers in IBC, place the load components into those positions of RHSG. Skip if equation number is -1 (restrained DOF).

main_program.description: The top-level solve sequence. Identical structure across all 3 notebooks.

nb01.code:
nodes, mats, elements, loads = readin()
DME, IBC, neq = DME(nodes, elements)
KG = assembly(elements, mats, nodes, neq, DME)
RHSG = loadasem(loads, IBC, neq, 3)
UG = np.linalg.solve(KG, RHSG)
print(UG)

nb02.code:
nodes, mats, elements, loads = readin()
DME, IBC, neq = DME(nodes, elements)
KG = assembly(elements, mats, nodes, neq, DME)
RHSG = loadasem(loads, IBC, neq, 1)
UG = np.linalg.solve(KG, RHSG)
print(UG)

nb03.code:
nodes, mats, elements, loads = readin()
DME, IBC, neq = DME(nodes, elements)
KG = assembly(elements, mats, nodes, neq, DME)
RHSG = loadasem(loads, IBC, neq, 1)
UG = np.linalg.solve(KG, RHSG)
print(UG)

main_program.cross_module_narrative: The main program is character-for-character identical across all 3 notebooks (except the number of loads). This is the ultimate payoff: readin → DME → assembly → load → solve is the SAME pipeline regardless of element type. The element-specific logic is entirely encapsulated in the uelXXX function. This is the power of the direct stiffness method — the algorithm is universal.
